### direct-connect-active-active-same-community-tag

### direct-connect-backup-vpn-bandwidth-limit-not-above-1-gbps

**Claim.** Site-to-Site VPN supports up to 1.25 Gbps throughput per tunnel and does not support ECMP for the egress path across several tunnels on the same virtual private gateway, so AWS does not recommend a VPN as the backup for Direct Connect connections faster than 1 Gbps.

**Write it as.** `we do not recommend customers use AWS Site to Site VPN as a backup for AWS Direct Connect connections with speeds greater than 1 Gbps` · `up to 1.25 Gbps throughput per VPN tunnel`

**Scope.** VPN backup for Direct Connect, virtual private gateway.

> "It is important to understand that AWS Site to Site VPN supports up to 1.25 Gbps throughput per VPN tunnel and does not support Equal Cost Multi Path (ECMP) for egress data path in the case of multiple AWS Site to Site VPN tunnels terminating on the same VGW. Thus, we do not recommend customers use AWS Site to Site VPN as a backup for AWS Direct Connect connections with speeds greater than 1 Gbps."
> — [AWS Direct Connect | Create resilient hybrid networks | AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/resiliency-recommendation/)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### direct-connect-backup-vpn-not-recommended-for-critical-workloads-cost-note

**Claim.** Combining Direct Connect as the primary path with a Site-to-Site VPN over the internet as backup is technically feasible and very cost effective, but it has technical downsides and can be more difficult to manage. AWS does not recommend it for highly critical or critical workloads.

AWS doesn’t recommend this for highly critical or critical workloads."

**Claim.** A Site-to-Site VPN ending on a transit gateway can be a cost-effective backup for Direct Connect; ECMP across multiple VPN tunnels allows throughput up to 50Gbps, even though each tunnel is capped at 1.25 Gbps, and Direct Connect is still the most effective choice for stable connectivity.

**Write it as.** `as a cost-effective backup` · `throughput of up to 50Gbps`

**Scope.** VPN backup on a transit gateway.

> "You can also consider AWS Site-to-Site VPN ending on an AWS Transit Gateway as a cost-effective backup to your primary AWS Direct Connect connection. It's important to note, however, that AWS Direct Connect is still the most effective choice for minimizing network disruptions and providing stable connectivity."

### direct-connect-backup-vpn-vpc-traffic-fails-over-automatically

**Claim.** If you configured a backup IPsec VPN connection, all VPC traffic fails over to the VPN automatically, and traffic to public resources such as Amazon S3 goes over the internet. Without a backup Direct Connect link or IPsec VPN link, Amazon VPC traffic is dropped when the connection fails.

**Write it as.** `will failover to the VPN connection automatically` · `Amazon VPC traffic will be dropped`

**Scope.** Direct Connect failure with and without a backup.

> "If you have configured a backup IPsec VPN connection instead, all VPC traffic will failover to the VPN connection automatically. Traffic to/from public resources, such as Amazon S3, will be routed over the internet. If you do not have a backup AWS Direct Connect link or an IPsec VPN link, then Amazon VPC traffic will be dropped in the event of a failure. Traffic to/from public resources will be routed over the internet."
> — [AWS Direct Connect | FAQ | Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/faqs/)

**Claim.** Direct Connect delivers data through a private network connection between your facilities and AWS instead of the internet. In many circumstances, private connections can reduce costs, increase bandwidth, and give a more consistent network experience than internet-based connections.

**Write it as.** `a more consistent network experience` · `private network connection between your facilities and AWS` · `an alternative to using the internet`

**Scope.** AWS Direct Connect compared with internet-based connections.

> "AWS Direct Connect is a networking service that provides an alternative to using the internet to connect to AWS. Using AWS Direct Connect, data that would have previously been transported over the internet is delivered through a private network connection between your facilities and AWS. In many circumstances, private network connections can reduce costs, increase bandwidth, and provide a more consistent network experience than internet-based connections."
> — [AWS Direct Connect | FAQ | Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://aws.amazon.com/directconnect/faqs/)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.
